# Feature Flag Sample (TypeScript)

This sample application shows how to use the Feature Flags.

## Prerequisites

The samples are compatible with [LTS versions of Node.js](https://github.com/nodejs/release#release-schedule).

You need [an Azure subscription][freesub] and the following resources created to run this sample:

### Create an App Configuration resource

You can use the [Azure Portal](https://portal.azure.com) or the [Azure CLI](https://learn.microsoft.com/cli/azure) to create an Azure App Configuration resource.

Example (Azure CLI):

```
az appconfig create --name <app-configuration-resource-name> --resource-group <resource-group-name> --location eastus
```

### Create an AAD application

We recommend the [@azure/identity][identity] package which provides a set of credential implementations for both NodeJS and the browser. This sample imports `InteractiveBrowserCredential` from identity.

- Register a new AAD application and give permissions to access Azure App Configuration on behalf of the signed-in user

  - Register a new application in the Azure Active Directory(in the azure-portal) - https://learn.microsoft.com/azure/active-directory/develop/quickstart-register-app
  - In the `API permissions` section, select `Add a permission` and choose `APIs my organization uses`.
  - Pick `Azure App Configuration` and select the checkboxes and then click `Add permissions`. This would allow the application to access Azure App Configuration on behalf of the signed-in user.

- Grant access to Azure App Configuration data with RBAC in the Azure Portal

  - RBAC roles for azure-app-configuration - https://learn.microsoft.com/azure/azure-app-configuration/concept-enable-rbac#azure-built-in-roles-for-azure-app-configuration.
  - In the azure portal, go to your app-config account and assign **App Configuration Data Owner** role to the registered AAD application from `Access control (IAM)` tab (in the left-side-navbar of your app config account in the azure-portal).

## Running the sample

1. Have the environment variables in sample.env populated in the .env file.

2. Create the following feature flags using the portal.

   ```json
   // Feature flag 1
   {
      "id": "react-app-feature-1",
      "description": "",
      "enabled": false,
      "conditions": {
        "client_filters": []
      }
   }
   // Feature flag 2 // Make sure to update the Start and End times as you wish.
   {
      "id": "react-app-feature-2",
      "description": "",
      "enabled": true,
      "conditions": {
        "client_filters": [
          {
            "name": "Microsoft.TimeWindow",
            "parameters": {
              "Start": "Mon, 12 Apr 2021 07:00:00 GMT",
              "End": "Wed, 14 Apr 2021 07:00:00 GMT"
            }
          }
        ]
      }
   }
   ```

3. Install the various packages as well as the TypeScript compiler using:

   ```bash
   npm install
   ```

4. Run the sample app:

   ```bash
   npm start
   ```

## Caution

> > This sample retrieves feature flags from a client-side application, however scalability can become a problem.
>
> > Azure App Configuration has a request quota detailed [here](https://azure.microsoft.com/pricing/details/app-configuration/). Once the quota is exhausted, HTTP status code 429 will be returned for all requests until the end of the hour.
>
> > For production environments and for users with heavy loads(keeping Azure costs in mind), the recommendation is to use App Configuration on the server-side and let the server cache and pass feature-flags to the clients.

## Next Steps

Take a look at our [Samples][samples] for more information about the APIs that are available.

[react]: https://create-react-app.dev/
[typescript]: https://www.typescriptlang.org/docs/home.html
[freesub]: https://azure.microsoft.com/free
[samples]: https://github.com/Azure/azure-sdk-for-js/blob/main/sdk/appconfiguration/app-configuration/samples/v1/typescript
[identity]: https://github.com/Azure/azure-sdk-for-js/blob/main/sdk/identity/identity/README.md

proposals.subtype: Request-body hash and canonical HMAC authentication
proposals.explanation: The policy hashes the request body's string representation, signs method, path/query, date, host and content hash, then sets x-ms-date, x-ms-content-sha256 and HMAC-SHA256 Authorization before forwarding.
proposals.handwrittenRationale: This separate credential module is explicitly installed by the outer client's connection-string branch while that client delegates operations to a differently named generated client.

proposals.subtype: Connection-string/token constructor adapter and policy assembly
proposals.explanation: The constructor selects token or parsed connection-string authentication, trims a trailing slash in the token branch, derives scopes, rejects unmatched connection strings, creates a generated client with an undefined credential in the HMAC branch, and installs audience, signing, query, empty-body and sync-token policies. It also builds SDK user-agent/logging options and selects the API version from the third options argument or its constant.
proposals.handwrittenRationale: The public AppConfigurationClient contains an explicit GeneratedAppConfigurationClient field and constructs the imported ./generated/appConfigurationClient implementation rather than being that generated class.

proposals.subtype: Create-only typed setting wrapper with 412 message normalization
proposals.explanation: addConfigurationSetting serializes typed values, encodes the key, calls generated putKeyValue with an initial ifNoneMatch '*', applies updated options and skipUrlEncoding, transforms the response, and rewrites a 412 error message inside a tracing span. The updated-options spread follows ifNoneMatch and can override it.
proposals.handwrittenRationale: The outer client's method explicitly adapts public setting types to its generated client's putKeyValue method.

proposals.subtype: Conditional delete with status-bearing response adaptation
proposals.explanation: deleteConfigurationSetting forwards an encoded key and label, maps conditional ETag options, captures HTTP status through onResponse, and transforms/asserts the generated result within a tracing span.
proposals.handwrittenRationale: The handwritten outer-client adapter calls a distinct generated deleteKeyValue operation and applies local response helpers.

proposals.subtype: Conditional get with explicit not-modified response shaping
proposals.explanation: getConfigurationSetting adapts fields, datetime and ETags around generated getKeyValue. On a caught 304 it builds a status-bearing result from the captured raw response, restores the requested key and clears non-HTTP setting members rather than rethrowing; other errors propagate. Execution is wrapped in a tracing span.
proposals.handwrittenRationale: This is an outer public method over generated getKeyValue with explicit 304 conversion and local model adapters.

proposals.subtype: Per-page ETags with next-link and 304 continuation
proposals.explanation: listConfigurationSettings copies then deletes options.pageEtags, consumes one ETag per request, transforms returned items and derives continuation from nextLink. A 304 becomes an empty page carrying the requested ETag and raw status while continuation comes from the error's Link header.
proposals.handwrittenRationale: The outer client builds its own PagedResult/getPage adapter using local transformation/token helpers, separately from imported generated operations.

proposals.subtype: Header-only page checking with conditional continuation
proposals.explanation: checkConfigurationSettings copies/deletes pageEtags, consumes one per request, exposes empty item pages with ETag from response headers and continuation from Link, and converts caught 304 responses to empty pages carrying the requested ETag and error-header continuation.
proposals.handwrittenRationale: The public outer-client method constructs a distinct custom PagedResult instead of exposing a generated pager directly.

proposals.subtype: Typed feature-flag value to JSON-string setting
proposals.explanation: The helper rejects a falsy value, prefixes unprefixed keys, supplies an ID from the key when absent, maps camelCase fields to the JSON schema, defaults requirement_type to Any and JSON-stringifies the value.
proposals.handwrittenRationale: This feature helper sits outside the generated subtree and is called by the internal adapter that converts public setting types to generated KeyValue operations; the public client explicitly accepts FeatureFlagValue.

proposals.subtype: Feature-flag JSON parsing and public shape normalization
proposals.explanation: parseFeatureFlag checks the setting predicate, parses JSON, ensures a key prefix, maps display_name and condition fields, defaults enabled to false and missing conditions to an empty filter list, and returns the fixed feature-flag content type.
proposals.handwrittenRationale: This exported convenience parser belongs to the feature module consumed by the outer generated-client adapter, not to the generated models/operations imports.

proposals.subtype: Content-type/string-value feature-flag type guard
proposals.explanation: isFeatureFlag recognizes a truthy setting with the exact feature-flag content type and a string value; it does not validate that string as JSON or require a key prefix.
proposals.handwrittenRationale: The predicate is exported alongside the public parser from the separate feature helper module, in a library with an explicitly separate generated client subtree.

proposals.subtype: Audience-configuration-specific credential error replacement
proposals.explanation: The policy replaces caught errors whose string message contains AADSTS500011 with one of two RestErrors depending on whether an audience was configured; all other errors are rethrown.
proposals.handwrittenRationale: The internal policy is explicitly installed by the outer client before its auth policy in the Sign phase.

proposals.subtype: Backfill absent or zero-length response bodies
proposals.explanation: After forwarding the request, emptyBodyPolicy replaces undefined, null or zero-length bodyAsText with '{}', without checking status or method. Nonempty text is preserved.
proposals.handwrittenRationale: This internal policy is separately added to the generated client's pipeline by the handwritten outer client.

proposals.subtype: Mutually exclusive conditional options and ETag quoting
proposals.explanation: The adapter rejects simultaneous truthy onlyIfChanged/onlyIfUnchanged, maps them to ifNoneMatch/ifMatch, and quotes ETags unless undefined, '*' or already enclosed in matching single/double quotes.
proposals.handwrittenRationale: The internal helper adapts public conditional-option names for the outer client's generated delete/get calls.

proposals.subtype: Public list filters to generated wire options
proposals.explanation: formatFiltersAndSelect renames keyFilter/labelFilter, URI-encodes each tag filter, ISO-formats a truthy acceptDateTime and converts selected public fields for generated request options.
proposals.handwrittenRationale: The internal helper explicitly returns a Pick of imported generated GetKeyValuesOptionalParams while accepting public ListRevisionsOptions.

proposals.subtype: Snapshot-name extension of setting filters
proposals.explanation: formatConfigurationSettingsFiltersAndSelect removes snapshotName from the input passed to the common filter adapter and exposes it as the generated snapshot option.
proposals.handwrittenRationale: This internal adapter converts the outer client's public SendConfigurationSettingsOptions to generated GetKeyValuesOptionalParams.

proposals.subtype: Snapshot filter names mapped to generated options
proposals.explanation: formatSnapshotFiltersAndSelect maps nameFilter, statusFilter and fields to name, status and select. The status/field casts do not perform runtime value conversion.
proposals.handwrittenRationale: The internal helper bridges public ListSnapshotsOptions and imported generated GetSnapshotsOptionalParams.

proposals.subtype: Label filter names mapped to generated options
proposals.explanation: formatLabelsFiltersAndSelect returns name from nameFilter and select from fields.
proposals.handwrittenRationale: This internal helper adapts public ListLabelsOptions to imported generated GetLabelsOptionalParams.

proposals.subtype: Public Date option to generated acceptDatetime string
proposals.explanation: formatAcceptDateTime returns acceptDatetime as the input Date's ISO string when truthy, preserving an undefined input through the short-circuit expression.
proposals.handwrittenRationale: The internal helper is used by the handwritten getConfigurationSetting wrapper before generated getKeyValue.

proposals.subtype: Extract and decode after token
proposals.explanation: extractAfterTokenFromNextLink feeds the supplied string directly to URLSearchParams, reads after, throws if missing/array-valued, and applies decodeURIComponent to the value. No URL normalization beyond this code is claimed.
proposals.handwrittenRationale: This internal continuation adapter is called by the handwritten public page iterator rather than a generated paging helper.

proposals.subtype: Link-header prefix to after-token adapter
proposals.explanation: extractAfterTokenFromLinkHeader takes the first semicolon-delimited segment, removes its first and last characters, then delegates token extraction. It does not search for a rel=next entry among multiple links.
proposals.handwrittenRationale: The internal helper supports the outer client's explicit 304/header-only page paths.

proposals.subtype: Clear setting data on empty conditional response
proposals.explanation: makeConfigurationSettingEmpty assigns undefined to contentType, description, etag, label, lastModified, isReadOnly, tags and value, preserving key and HTTP-related members. Despite its comment it does not install throwing getters.
proposals.handwrittenRationale: This internal model adapter is explicitly invoked by the outer client's getConfigurationSetting 304 path.

proposals.subtype: Generated KeyValue to public ConfigurationSetting
proposals.explanation: transformKeyValue spreads the wire value, defaults value to undefined before that spread, exposes boolean isReadOnly from locked, converts a truthy lastModified with new Date, removes locked, and deletes falsy label/contentType.
proposals.handwrittenRationale: The internal function explicitly adapts an imported generated KeyValue into a distinct public ConfigurationSetting type.

proposals.subtype: Content-type-directed typed-value serialization with fallback
proposals.explanation: The dispatcher passes string/undefined/null values through, routes nonstring defined values by feature/secret/snapshot content type, returns the original setting if a helper throws, and otherwise logs then throws TypeError for an unsupported typed value.
proposals.handwrittenRationale: These internal predicates and dispatcher bridge the outer client's typed input union and its generated putKeyValue entity.

proposals.subtype: Status-bearing setting response with hidden raw metadata
proposals.explanation: transformKeyValueResponseWithStatusCode transforms the supplied wire value or an empty object, supplies statusCode with -1 fallback, and defines nonenumerable _response when it is an own property of the source.
proposals.handwrittenRationale: The internal helper adds the outer client's public HTTP response shape to generated KeyValue results.

proposals.subtype: Setting response adaptation and eTag removal
proposals.explanation: transformKeyValueResponse applies the public-model conversion, installs nonenumerable _response when present on the input, and deletes the alternate eTag property.
proposals.handwrittenRationale: The internal helper is a public-response adapter used after the outer client's generated putKeyValue call.

proposals.subtype: Snapshot date/count adaptation and raw response preservation
proposals.explanation: transformSnapshotResponse spreads the generated snapshot, converts truthy createdOn/expiresOn values to Dates, adds itemCount from itemsCount, and preserves _response nonenumerably when present. It does not remove the spread itemsCount property.
proposals.handwrittenRationale: The internal helper explicitly converts the imported generated Snapshot type to the outer client's public ConfigurationSnapshot/SnapshotResponse.

proposals.subtype: Public selected-field names to wire enum names
proposals.explanation: formatFieldsForSelect maps lastModified/contentType/isReadOnly to last_modified/content_type/locked, passes other names through and returns undefined for nullish input.
proposals.handwrittenRationale: The internal helper bridges keys of the public ConfigurationSetting and the generated KeyValueFields type.

proposals.subtype: Own-property response assertion with diagnostic placeholder
proposals.explanation: hasUnderscoreResponse checks an own _response property. assertResponse defines a nonenumerable diagnostic string when absent; it neither throws nor fabricates an HTTP response object.
proposals.handwrittenRationale: These internal helpers assert the outer client's public response contract after its custom generated-result adapters.

proposals.subtype: Explicit audience or endpoint-derived cloud scope
proposals.explanation: getScope appends /.default to a truthy explicit audience; otherwise it recognizes staging or the rightmost appconfig/azconfig hostname label and its suffix, with AzurePublicCloud fallback.
proposals.handwrittenRationale: The internal helper is called by the outer client's token-credential constructor before constructing its explicitly separate generated client.

proposals.subtype: Additional RFC3986 path-character escaping
proposals.explanation: encodePathParameter applies encodeURIComponent then percent-encodes !, single quote, (, ) and * using uppercase hex; the outer client disables generated URL encoding for these already encoded keys.
proposals.handwrittenRationale: The internal helper is explicitly used by the outer client's generated-operation wrappers together with skipUrlEncoding.
